summary: The destruction of Assyria is a type of the destruction of the wicked at the Second Coming—Few people will be left after the Lord comes again—The remnant of Jacob will return in that day—Compare 2 Nephi 20.
meta_description: The destruction of Assyria is a type of the destruction of the wicked at the Second Coming—Few people will be left after the Lord comes again—The remnant of Jacob will return in that day—Compare 2 Nephi 20.

footnotes.note5_a: OR Assyria is the rod of my anger, and my wrath is a staff in their hand. Ezek. 31:3.
footnotes.note7_a: HEB did his heart intend it thus.
footnotes.note15_a: All the metaphors in this verse ask the same question: Can man (e.g., the Assyrian king) prosper against God?
footnotes.note16_b: IE of the king of Assyria (also vv. 17–19).
footnotes.note20_a: This prophecy extends to the latter days in the succeeding verse.
footnotes.note22_c: IE even when punishment comes, mercy is available.
footnotes.note24_b: IE as the Egyptians did in earlier times.
footnotes.note28_a: Progress of the Assyrian armies toward Jerusalem is traced; then (vv. 33–34) the Lord’s action against them is figuratively described.
footnotes.note33_a: See Isa. 36–37 or 2 Kgs. 18:13–19:37 for a fulfillment of this prophecy.
